# California Contractor Deposit Dispute: Practical Next Steps

A missed completion date after a **USD 2,000 deposit** is often handled best by building a clean paper trail first, then sending a short written demand, and only then preparing for small claims if the refund is not made.

## Checklist to Build Your Case and Ask for a Refund

| Step | What to do | What to keep |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Gather the contract and all written terms | Signed agreement, estimate, scope of work, start/completion dates, payment terms |
| 2 | Save proof of payment | Receipt, bank transfer, canceled check, card statement, deposit confirmation |
| 3 | Document the missed deadline | Calendar notes, texts/emails showing the agreed completion date of **2025-10-20** and any delays |
| 4 | Create a communication log | Dates, times, who said what, and screenshots of calls/texts/emails |
| 5 | Photograph the job status | Before/after photos, unfinished work, materials on site, damage if any |
| 6 | Calculate your loss | Deposit amount, any extra costs, temporary repairs, replacement contractor quotes |
| 7 | Send a written demand | Ask for a refund by a firm deadline and keep a copy |
| 8 | Prepare for small claims | Organize exhibits, witnesses, and a simple timeline |

### Records to Gather
- Signed contract, estimate, change orders, invoices
- Proof of the **USD 2,000** deposit and the date paid: **2025-09-15**
- Texts, emails, voicemail transcripts, and letters
- Photos/videos of the work site and unfinished work
- Any promises about completion, materials, permits, or start dates
- Receipts for substitute work, repairs, or mitigation
- Contractor’s full legal name, business name, address, phone, email, and license number if available

## Demand Letter and Small Claims Prep

### What to Write in the Demand Letter
Keep it short, factual, and calm. Include:
- Your name and contact information
- Contractor’s name/business name and mailing address
- Project address
- Deposit amount: **USD 2,000**
- Date paid: **2025-09-15**
- Agreed completion date: **2025-10-20**
- Brief description of the missed deadline and unfinished work
- A clear request: refund the deposit, or the unpaid portion if only part of the work was done
- A firm deadline to respond or pay, usually 7–14 days
- How payment should be made
- A statement that you will consider small claims court if the matter is not resolved

### Demand Letter Structure
- Opening: identify the project and contract
- Facts: payment date, promised completion date, what was missed
- Demand: exact amount requested and by when
- Delivery: send by a trackable method and keep proof
- Tone: professional, specific, non-threatening

### Small Claims Court Prep
- Build a one-page timeline of events
- Organize exhibits in order: contract, payment proof, messages, photos, demand letter, delivery proof
- Bring copies for the court, the contractor, and yourself
- Be ready to explain:
  - What was agreed
  - What was paid
  - What was missed
  - What you asked for before filing
  - How you calculated the amount you want back

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

- Waiting too long to document the problem
- Relying on phone calls without written follow-up
- Sending a demand letter without a deadline
- Mixing emotions into the letter instead of sticking to facts
- Throwing away receipts, screenshots, or photos
- Changing the story later; keep your timeline consistent
- Asking for vague relief instead of a specific refund amount
- Not checking the contractor’s exact legal business name
- Failing to keep proof that the demand letter was delivered
- Doing major replacement work before documenting the unfinished condition

## Quick Actions

- Action: [Button: Draft demand] https://www.courts.ca.gov/selfhelp-smallclaims.htm
- Action: [Button: Small claims info] https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/small-claims
- Action: [Button: Contractor lookup] https://www.cslb.ca.gov/OnlineServices/CheckLicenseII/CheckLicense.aspx

## Sources

- California Courts Self-Help, Small Claims: https://www.courts.ca.gov/selfhelp-smallclaims.htm
- California Self-Help Guide, Small Claims: https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/small-claims
- California Contractors State License Board license check: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/OnlineServices/CheckLicenseII/CheckLicense.aspx
